units.leftText: If one part suffers, every part suffers with it; if one part is honored, every part rejoices with it. The Greater Gifts
units.rightText: And whether one member suffereth, all the members suffer with it; or one member is honored, all the members rejoice with it.

units.leftText: Now you are the body of Christ, and each of you is a member of it.
units.rightText: Now ye are the body of Christ, and severally members thereof.

units.leftText: And in the church God has appointed first of all apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then workers of miracles, and those with gifts of healing, helping, administration, and various tongues.
units.rightText: And God hath set some in the church, first apostles, secondly prophets, thirdly teachers, then miracles, then gifts of healings, helps, governments, divers kinds of tongues.

units.leftText: Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Do all work miracles?
units.rightText: Are all apostles? are all prophets? are all teachers? are all workers of miracles?

units.leftText: Do all have gifts of healing? Do all speak in tongues? Do all interpret?
units.rightText: have all gifts of healings? do all speak with tongues? do all interpret?

units.leftText: But eagerly desire the greater gifts. And now I will show you the most excellent way.
units.rightText: But desire earnestly the greater gifts. And moreover a most excellent way show I unto you.

units.leftText: If I speak in the tongues of men and of angels, but have not love, I am only a ringing gong or a clanging cymbal.
units.rightText: If I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, but have not love, I am become sounding brass, or a clanging cymbal.

units.leftText: If I have the gift of prophecy and can fathom all mysteries and all knowledge, and if I have absolute faith so as to move mountains, but have not love, I am nothing.
units.rightText: And if I have the gift of prophecy, and know all mysteries and all knowledge; and if I have all faith, so as to remove mountains, but have not love, I am nothing.

units.leftText: If I give all I possess to the poor and exult in the surrender of my body, but have not love, I gain nothing.
units.rightText: And if I bestow all my goods to feed the poor, and if I give my body to be burned, but have not love, it profiteth me nothing.
leftNotes: 13:3 SBL, NE, BYZ, and TR surrender my body to be burned

units.leftText: Love is patient, love is kind. It does not envy, it does not boast, it is not proud.
units.rightText: Love suffereth long, and is kind; love envieth not; love vaunteth not itself, is not puffed up,

units.leftText: It is not rude, it is not self-seeking, it is not easily angered, it keeps no account of wrongs.
units.rightText: doth not behave itself unseemly, seeketh not its own, is not provoked, taketh not account of evil;

units.leftText: Love takes no pleasure in evil, but rejoices in the truth.
units.rightText: rejoiceth not in unrighteousness, but rejoiceth with the truth;

units.leftText: It bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things.
units.rightText: beareth all things, believeth all things, hopeth all things, endureth all things.

units.leftText: Love never fails. But where there are prophecies, they will cease; where there are tongues, they will be restrained; where there is knowledge, it will be dismissed.
units.rightText: Love never faileth: but whether there be prophecies, they shall be done away; whether there be tongues, they shall cease; whether there be knowledge, it shall be done away.

units.leftText: For we know in part and we prophesy in part,
units.rightText: For we know in part, and we prophesy in part;

units.leftText: but when the perfect comes, the partial passes away.
units.rightText: but when that which is perfect is come, that which is in part shall be done away.

units.leftText: When I was a child, I talked like a child, I thought like a child, I reasoned like a child. When I became a man, I set aside childish ways.
units.rightText: When I was a child, I spake as a child, I felt as a child, I thought as a child: now that I am become a man, I have put away childish things.

units.leftText: Now we see but a dim reflection as in a mirror; then we shall see face to face. Now I know in part; then I shall know fully, even as I am fully known.
units.rightText: For now we see in a mirror, darkly; but then face to face: now I know in part; but then shall I know fully even as also I was fully known.

units.leftText: And now these three remain: faith, hope, and love; but the greatest of these is love.
units.rightText: But now abideth faith, hope, love, these three; and the greatest of these is love.

units.leftText: Earnestly pursue love and eagerly desire spiritual gifts, especially the gift of prophecy.
units.rightText: Follow after love; yet desire earnestly spiritual gifts, but rather that ye may prophesy.

units.leftText: For he who speaks in a tongue does not speak to men, but to God. Indeed, no one understands him; he utters mysteries in the Spirit.
units.rightText: For he that speaketh in a tongue speaketh not unto men, but unto God; for no man understandeth; but in the spirit he speaketh mysteries.

units.leftText: But he who prophesies speaks to men for their edification, encouragement, and comfort.
units.rightText: But he that prophesieth speaketh unto men edification, and exhortation, and consolation.

units.leftText: The one who speaks in a tongue edifies himself, but the one who prophesies edifies the church.
units.rightText: He that speaketh in a tongue edifieth himself; but he that prophesieth edifieth the church.

units.leftText: I wish that all of you could speak in tongues, but I would rather have you prophesy. He who prophesies is greater than one who speaks in tongues, unless he interprets so that the church may be edified.
units.rightText: Now I would have you all speak with tongues, but rather that ye should prophesy: and greater is he that prophesieth than he that speaketh with tongues, except he interpret, that the church may receive edifying.

units.leftText: Now, brothers, if I come to you speaking in tongues, how will I benefit you, unless I bring you some revelation or knowledge or prophecy or teaching?
units.rightText: But now, brethren, if I come unto you speaking with tongues, what shall I profit you, unless I speak to you either by way of revelation, or of knowledge, or of prophesying, or of teaching?

units.leftText: Even in the case of lifeless instruments, such as the flute or harp, how will anyone recognize the tune they are playing unless the notes are distinct?
units.rightText: Even things without life, giving a voice, whether pipe or harp, if they give not a distinction in the sounds, how shall it be known what is piped or harped?

units.leftText: Again, if the trumpet sounds a muffled call, who will prepare for battle?
units.rightText: For if the trumpet give an uncertain voice, who shall prepare himself for war?

units.leftText: So it is with you. Unless you speak intelligible words with your tongue, how will anyone know what you are saying? You will just be speaking into the air.
units.rightText: So also ye, unless ye utter by the tongue speech easy to be understood, how shall it be known what is spoken? for ye will be speaking into the air.

units.leftText: Assuredly, there are many different languages in the world, yet none of them is without meaning.
units.rightText: There are, it may be, so many kinds of voices in the world, and no kind is without signification.

units.leftText: If, then, I do not know the meaning of someone’s language, I am a foreigner to the speaker, and he is a foreigner to me.
units.rightText: If then I know not the meaning of the voice, I shall be to him that speaketh a barbarian, and he that speaketh will be a barbarian unto me.
leftNotes: 14:11 Literally a barbarian; twice in this verse

units.leftText: It is the same with you. Since you are eager to have spiritual gifts, strive to excel in gifts that build up the church.
units.rightText: So also ye, since ye are zealous of spiritual gifts, seek that ye may abound unto the edifying of the church.

units.leftText: Therefore, the one who speaks in a tongue should pray that he may interpret.
units.rightText: Wherefore let him that speaketh in a tongue pray that he may interpret.

units.leftText: For if I pray in a tongue, my spirit prays, but my mind is unfruitful.
units.rightText: For if I pray in a tongue, my spirit prayeth, but my understanding is unfruitful.

units.leftText: What then shall I do? I will pray with my spirit, but I will also pray with my mind. I will sing with my spirit, but I will also sing with my mind.
units.rightText: What is it then? I will pray with the spirit, and I will pray with the understanding also: I will sing with the spirit, and I will sing with the understanding also.

units.leftText: Otherwise, if you speak a blessing in spirit, how can someone who is uninstructed say “Amen” to your thanksgiving, since he does not know what you are saying?
units.rightText: Else if thou bless with the spirit, how shall he that filleth the place of the unlearned say the Amen at thy giving of thanks, seeing he knoweth not what thou sayest?
leftNotes: 14:16 Or in the Spirit

units.leftText: You may be giving thanks well enough, but the other one is not edified.
units.rightText: For thou verily givest thanks well, but the other is not edified.

units.leftText: I thank God that I speak in tongues more than all of you.
units.rightText: I thank God, I speak with tongues more than you all:

units.leftText: But in the church, I would rather speak five coherent words to instruct others than ten thousand words in a tongue.
units.rightText: howbeit in the church I had rather speak five words with my understanding, that I might instruct others also, than ten thousand words in a tongue.

units.leftText: Brothers, stop thinking like children. In regard to evil be infants, but in your thinking be mature.
units.rightText: Brethren, be not children in mind: yet in malice be ye babes, but in mind be men.

units.leftText: It is written in the Law: “By strange tongues and foreign lips I will speak to this people, but even then they will not listen to Me, says the Lord.”
units.rightText: In the law it is written, By men of strange tongues and by the lips of strangers will I speak unto this people; and not even thus will they hear me, saith the Lord.

units.leftText: Tongues, then, are a sign, not for believers, but for unbelievers. Prophecy, however, is for believers, not for unbelievers.
units.rightText: Wherefore tongues are for a sign, not to them that believe, but to the unbelieving: but prophesying is for a sign, not to the unbelieving, but to them that believe.

units.leftText: So if the whole church comes together and everyone speaks in tongues, and some who are uninstructed or some unbelievers come in, will they not say that you are out of your minds?
units.rightText: If therefore the whole church be assembled together and all speak with tongues, and there come in men unlearned or unbelieving, will they not say that ye are mad?

units.leftText: But if an unbeliever or uninstructed person comes in while everyone is prophesying, he will be convicted and called to account by all,
units.rightText: But if all prophesy, and there come in one unbelieving or unlearned, he is reproved by all, he is judged by all;

units.leftText: and the secrets of his heart will be made known. So he will fall facedown and worship God, proclaiming, “God is truly among you!” Orderly Worship
units.rightText: the secrets of his heart are made manifest; and so he will fall down on his face and worship God, declaring that God is among you indeed.

units.leftText: What then shall we say, brothers? When you come together, everyone has a psalm or a teaching, a revelation, a tongue, or an interpretation. All of these must be done to build up the church.
units.rightText: What is it then, brethren? When ye come together, each one hath a psalm, hath a teaching, hath a revelation, hath a tongue, hath an interpretation. Let all things be done unto edifying.

units.leftText: If anyone speaks in a tongue, two, or at most three, should speak in turn, and someone must interpret.
units.rightText: If any man speaketh in a tongue, let it be by two, or at the most three, and that in turn; and let one interpret:

units.leftText: But if there is no interpreter, he should remain silent in the church and speak only to himself and God.
units.rightText: but if there be no interpreter, let him keep silence in the church; and let him speak to himself, and to God.

units.leftText: Two or three prophets should speak, and the others should weigh carefully what is said.
units.rightText: And let the prophets speak by two or three, and let the others discern.

units.leftText: And if a revelation comes to someone who is seated, the first speaker should stop.
units.rightText: But if a revelation be made to another sitting by, let the first keep silence.

units.leftText: For you can all prophesy in turn so that everyone may be instructed and encouraged.
units.rightText: For ye all can prophesy one by one, that all may learn, and all may be exhorted;

units.leftText: The spirits of prophets are subject to prophets.
units.rightText: and the spirits of the prophets are subject to the prophets;

units.leftText: For God is not a God of disorder, but of peace— as in all the churches of the saints.
units.rightText: for God is not a God of confusion, but of peace. As in all the churches of the saints,
leftNotes: 14:33 Or of peace. As in all the churches of the saints: Thus, some translators begin the new paragraph after peace.

units.leftText: Women are to be silent in the churches. They are not permitted to speak, but must be in submission, as the law says.
units.rightText: let the women keep silence in the churches: for it is not permitted unto them to speak; but let them be in subjection, as also saith the law.

units.leftText: If they wish to inquire about something, they are to ask their own husbands at home; for it is dishonorable for a woman to speak in the church.
units.rightText: And if they would learn anything, let them ask their own husbands at home: for it is shameful for a woman to speak in the church.
leftNotes: 14:35 Some manuscripts place verses 34–35 after verse 40.

units.leftText: Did the word of God originate with you? Or are you the only ones it has reached?
units.rightText: What? was it from you that the word of God went forth? or came it unto you alone?

units.leftText: If anyone considers himself a prophet or spiritual person, let him acknowledge that what I am writing you is the Lord’s command.
units.rightText: If any man thinketh himself to be a prophet, or spiritual, let him take knowledge of the things which I write unto you, that they are the commandment of the Lord.

units.leftText: But if anyone ignores this, he himself will be ignored.
units.rightText: But if any man is ignorant, let him be ignorant.
leftNotes: 14:38 BYZ and TR let him be ignorant

units.leftText: So, my brothers, be eager to prophesy, and do not forbid speaking in tongues.
units.rightText: Wherefore, my brethren, desire earnestly to prophesy, and forbid not to speak with tongues.

units.leftText: But everything must be done in a proper and orderly manner.
units.rightText: But let all things be done decently and in order.

units.leftText: Now, brothers, I want to remind you of the gospel I preached to you, which you received, and in which you stand firm.
units.rightText: Now I make known unto you brethren, the gospel which I preached unto you, which also ye received, wherein also ye stand,

units.leftText: By this gospel you are saved, if you hold firmly to the word I preached to you. Otherwise, you have believed in vain.
units.rightText: by which also ye are saved, if ye hold fast the word which I preached unto you, except ye believed in vain.

units.leftText: For what I received I passed on to you as of first importance: that Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures,
units.rightText: For I delivered unto you first of all that which also I received: that Christ died for our sins according to the scriptures;

units.leftText: that He was buried, that He was raised on the third day according to the Scriptures,
units.rightText: and that he was buried; and that he hath been raised on the third day according to the scriptures;

units.leftText: and that He appeared to Cephas and then to the Twelve.
units.rightText: and that he appeared to Cephas; then to the twelve;
leftNotes: 15:5 That is, Peter

units.leftText: After that, He appeared to more than five hundred brothers at once, most of whom are still living, though some have fallen asleep.
units.rightText: then he appeared to above five hundred brethren at once, of whom the greater part remain until now, but some are fallen asleep;

units.leftText: Then He appeared to James, then to all the apostles.
units.rightText: then he appeared to James; then to all the apostles;

units.leftText: And last of all He appeared to me also, as to one of untimely birth.
units.rightText: and last of all, as to the child untimely born, he appeared to me also.

units.leftText: For I am the least of the apostles and am unworthy to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the church of God.
units.rightText: For I am the least of the apostles, that am not meet to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the church of God.

units.leftText: But by the grace of God I am what I am, and His grace to me was not in vain. No, I worked harder than all of them — yet not I, but the grace of God that was with me.
units.rightText: But by the grace of God I am what I am: and his grace which was bestowed upon me was not found vain; but I labored more abundantly than they all: yet not I, but the grace of God which was with me.

units.leftText: Whether, then, it was I or they, this is what we preach, and this is what you believed. The Resurrection of the Dead
units.rightText: Whether then it be I or they, so we preach, and so ye believed.

units.leftText: But if it is preached that Christ has been raised from the dead, how can some of you say that there is no resurrection of the dead?
units.rightText: Now if Christ is preached that he hath been raised from the dead, how say some among you that there is no resurrection of the dead?

units.leftText: If there is no resurrection of the dead, then not even Christ has been raised.
units.rightText: But if there is no resurrection of the dead, neither hath Christ been raised:

units.leftText: And if Christ has not been raised, our preaching is worthless, and so is your faith.
units.rightText: and if Christ hath not been raised, then is our preaching vain, your faith also is vain.

units.leftText: In that case, we are also exposed as false witnesses about God. For we have testified about God that He raised Christ from the dead, but He did not raise Him if in fact the dead are not raised.
units.rightText: Yea, and we are found false witnesses of God; because we witnessed of God that he raised up Christ: whom he raised not up, if so be that the dead are not raised.

units.leftText: For if the dead are not raised, then not even Christ has been raised.
units.rightText: For if the dead are not raised, neither hath Christ been raised:

units.leftText: And if Christ has not been raised, your faith is futile; you are still in your sins.
units.rightText: and if Christ hath not been raised, your faith is vain; ye are yet in your sins.

units.leftText: Then those also who have fallen asleep in Christ have perished.
units.rightText: Then they also that are fallen asleep in Christ have perished.

units.leftText: If our hope in Christ is for this life alone, we are to be pitied more than all men. The Order of Resurrection
units.rightText: If we have only hoped in Christ in this life, we are of all men most pitiable.

units.leftText: But Christ has indeed been raised from the dead, the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep.
units.rightText: But now hath Christ been raised from the dead, the firstfruits of them that are asleep.

units.leftText: For since death came through a man, the resurrection of the dead comes also through a man.
units.rightText: For since by man came death, by man came also the resurrection of the dead.

units.leftText: For as in Adam all die, so in Christ all will be made alive.
units.rightText: For as in Adam all die, so also in Christ shall all be made alive.

units.leftText: But each in his own turn: Christ the firstfruits; then at His coming, those who belong to Him.
units.rightText: But each in his own order: Christ the firstfruits; then they that are Christ’s, at his coming.

units.leftText: Then the end will come, when He hands over the kingdom to God the Father after He has destroyed all dominion, authority, and power.
units.rightText: Then cometh the end, when he shall deliver up the kingdom to God, even the Father; when he shall have abolished all rule and all authority and power.

units.leftText: For He must reign until He has put all His enemies under His feet.
units.rightText: For he must reign, till he hath put all his enemies under his feet.

units.leftText: The last enemy to be destroyed is death.
units.rightText: The last enemy that shall be abolished is death.

units.leftText: For “God has put everything under His feet.” Now when it says that everything has been put under Him, this clearly does not include the One who put everything under Him.
units.rightText: For, He put all things in subjection under his feet. But when he saith, All things are put in subjection, it is evident that he is excepted who did subject all things unto him.

units.leftText: And when all things have been subjected to Him, then the Son Himself will be made subject to Him who put all things under Him, so that God may be all in all.
units.rightText: And when all things have been subjected unto him, then shall the Son also himself be subjected to him that did subject all things unto him, that God may be all in all.

units.leftText: If these things are not so, what will those do who are baptized for the dead? If the dead are not raised at all, why are people baptized for them?
units.rightText: Else what shall they do that are baptized for the dead? If the dead are not raised at all, why then are they baptized for them?

units.leftText: And why do we endanger ourselves every hour?
units.rightText: why do we also stand in jeopardy every hour?

units.leftText: I face death every day, brothers, as surely as I boast about you in Christ Jesus our Lord.
units.rightText: I protest by that glorying in you, brethren, which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord, I die daily.

units.leftText: If I fought wild beasts in Ephesus for human motives, what did I gain? If the dead are not raised, “Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die.”
units.rightText: If after the manner of men I fought with beasts at Ephesus, what doth it profit me? If the dead are not raised, let us eat and drink, for to-morrow we die.

units.leftText: Do not be deceived: “Bad company corrupts good character.”
units.rightText: Be not deceived: Evil companionships corrupt good morals.
leftNotes: 15:33 Probably a quote from the Greek comedy Thais by Menander

units.leftText: Sober up as you ought, and stop sinning; for some of you are ignorant of God. I say this to your shame. The Resurrection Body
units.rightText: Awake to soberness righteously, and sin not; for some have no knowledge of God: I speak this to move you to shame.

units.leftText: But someone will ask, “How are the dead raised? With what kind of body will they come?”
units.rightText: But some one will say, How are the dead raised? and with what manner of body do they come?

units.leftText: You fool! What you sow does not come to life unless it dies.
units.rightText: Thou foolish one, that which thou thyself sowest is not quickened except it die:

units.leftText: And what you sow is not the body that will be, but just a seed, perhaps of wheat or something else.
units.rightText: and that which thou sowest, thou sowest not the body that shall be, but a bare grain, it may chance of wheat, or of some other kind;

units.leftText: But God gives it a body as He has designed, and to each kind of seed He gives its own body.
units.rightText: but God giveth it a body even as it pleased him, and to each seed a body of its own.

units.leftText: Not all flesh is the same: Men have one kind of flesh, animals have another, birds another, and fish another.
units.rightText: All flesh is not the same flesh: but there is one flesh of men, and another flesh of beasts, and another flesh of birds, and another of fishes.

units.leftText: There are also heavenly bodies and earthly bodies. But the splendor of the heavenly bodies is of one degree, and the splendor of the earthly bodies is of another.
units.rightText: There are also celestial bodies, and bodies terrestrial: but the glory of the celestial is one, and the glory of the terrestrial is another.

units.leftText: The sun has one degree of splendor, the moon another, and the stars another; and star differs from star in splendor.
units.rightText: There is one glory of the sun, and another glory of the moon, and another glory of the stars; for one star differeth from another star in glory.

units.leftText: So will it be with the resurrection of the dead: What is sown is perishable; it is raised imperishable.
units.rightText: So also is the resurrection of the dead. It is sown in corruption; it is raised in incorruption:

units.leftText: It is sown in dishonor; it is raised in glory. It is sown in weakness; it is raised in power.
units.rightText: it is sown in dishonor; it is raised in glory: it is sown in weakness; it is raised in power:

units.leftText: It is sown a natural body; it is raised a spiritual body. If there is a natural body, there is also a spiritual body.
units.rightText: it is sown a natural body; it is raised a spiritual body. If there is a natural body, there is also a spiritual body.

units.leftText: So it is written: “The first man Adam became a living being”; the last Adam a life-giving spirit.
units.rightText: So also it is written, The first man Adam became a living soul. The last Adam became a life-giving spirit.
leftNotes: 15:45 Genesis 2:7|GEN 2:7*

units.leftText: The spiritual, however, was not first, but the natural, and then the spiritual.
units.rightText: Howbeit that is not first which is spiritual, but that which is natural; then that which is spiritual.

units.leftText: The first man was of the dust of the earth, the second man from heaven.
units.rightText: The first man is of the earth, earthy: the second man is of heaven.

units.leftText: As was the earthly man, so also are those who are of the earth; and as is the heavenly man, so also are those who are of heaven.
units.rightText: As is the earthy, such are they also that are earthy: and as is the heavenly, such are they also that are heavenly.

units.leftText: And just as we have borne the likeness of the earthly man, so also shall we bear the likeness of the heavenly man. Where, O Death, Is Your Victory? (Hosea 13:9–14|HOS 13:9-14*)
units.rightText: And as we have borne the image of the earthy, we shall also bear the image of the heavenly.

units.leftText: Now I declare to you, brothers, that flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God, nor does the perishable inherit the imperishable.
units.rightText: Now this I say, brethren, that flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God; neither doth corruption inherit incorruption.

units.leftText: Listen, I tell you a mystery: We will not all sleep, but we will all be changed —
units.rightText: Behold, I tell you a mystery: We all shall not sleep, but we shall all be changed,

units.leftText: in an instant, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet. For the trumpet will sound, the dead will be raised imperishable, and we will be changed.
units.rightText: in a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trump: for the trumpet shall sound, and the dead shall be raised incorruptible, and we shall be changed.

units.leftText: For the perishable must be clothed with the imperishable, and the mortal with immortality.
units.rightText: For this corruptible must put on incorruption, and this mortal must put on immortality.
leftNotes: 15:53 Or clothe itself

units.leftText: When the perishable has been clothed with the imperishable and the mortal with immortality, then the saying that is written will come to pass: “Death has been swallowed up in victory.”
units.rightText: But when this corruptible shall have put on incorruption, and this mortal shall have put on immortality, then shall come to pass the saying that is written, Death is swallowed up in victory.
leftNotes: 15:54 WH does not include and the mortal with immortality.

units.leftText: “Where, O Death, is your victory? Where, O Death, is your sting?”
units.rightText: O death, where is thy victory? O death, where is thy sting?
leftNotes: 15:55 Hosea 13:14|HOS 13:14* (see also LXX); BYZ and TR “Where, O Death, is your sting? Where, O Hades, is your victory?”

units.leftText: The sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the law.
units.rightText: The sting of death is sin; and the power of sin is the law:

units.leftText: But thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ!
units.rightText: but thanks be to God, who giveth us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.

units.leftText: Therefore, my beloved brothers, be steadfast and immovable. Always excel in the work of the Lord, because you know that your labor in the Lord is not in vain.
units.rightText: Wherefore, my beloved brethren, be ye stedfast, unmoveable, always abounding in the work of the Lord, forasmuch as ye know that your labor is not vain in the Lord.

units.leftText: Now about the collection for the saints, you are to do as I directed the churches of Galatia:
units.rightText: Now concerning the collection for the saints, as I gave order to the churches of Galatia, so also do ye.

units.leftText: On the first day of every week, each of you should set aside a portion of his income, saving it up, so that when I come no collections will be needed.
units.rightText: Upon the first day of the week let each one of you lay by him in store, as he may prosper, that no collections be made when I come.

units.leftText: Then, on my arrival, I will send letters with those you recommend to carry your gift to Jerusalem.
units.rightText: And when I arrive, whomsoever ye shall approve, them will I send with letters to carry your bounty unto Jerusalem:

units.leftText: And if it is advisable for me to go also, they can travel with me. Paul’s Travel Plans (Romans 15:23–33|ROM 15:23-33*)
units.rightText: and if it be meet for me to go also, they shall go with me.

units.leftText: After I go through Macedonia, however, I will come to you; for I will be going through Macedonia.
units.rightText: But I will come unto you, when I shall have passed through Macedonia; for I pass through Macedonia;

units.leftText: Perhaps I will stay with you awhile, or even spend the winter, so that you can help me on my journey, wherever I go.
units.rightText: but with you it may be that I shall abide, or even winter, that ye may set me forward on my journey whithersoever I go.

units.leftText: For I do not want to see you now only in passing; I hope to spend some time with you, if the Lord permits.
units.rightText: For I do not wish to see you now by the way; for I hope to tarry a while with you, if the Lord permit.

units.leftText: But I will stay in Ephesus until Pentecost,
units.rightText: But I will tarry at Ephesus until Pentecost;
leftNotes: 16:8 That is, Shavuot, the late spring feast of pilgrimage to Jerusalem; it is also known as the Feast of Harvest(see Exodus 23:16|EXO 23:16*) or the Feast of Weeks(see Exodus 34:22|EXO 34:22*).

units.leftText: because a great door for effective work has opened to me, even though many oppose me. Timothy and Apollos (Philippians 2:19–30|PHP 2:19-30*)
units.rightText: for a great door and effectual is opened unto me, and there are many adversaries.

units.leftText: If Timothy comes, see to it that he has nothing to fear while he is with you, for he is doing the work of the Lord, just as I am.
units.rightText: Now if Timothy come, see that he be with you without fear; for he worketh the work of the Lord, as I also do:

units.leftText: No one, then, should treat him with contempt. Send him on his way in peace so that he can return to me, for I am expecting him along with the brothers.
units.rightText: let no man therefore despise him. But set him forward on his journey in peace, that he may come unto me: for I expect him with the brethren.

units.leftText: Now about our brother Apollos: I strongly urged him to go to you with the brothers. He was not at all inclined to go now, but he will go when he has the opportunity. Concluding Exhortations
units.rightText: But as touching Apollos the brother, I besought him much to come unto you with the brethren: and it was not at all his will to come now; but he will come when he shall have opportunity.

units.leftText: Be on the alert. Stand firm in the faith. Be men of courage. Be strong.
units.rightText: Watch ye, stand fast in the faith, quit you like men, be strong.

units.leftText: Do everything in love.
units.rightText: Let all that ye do be done in love.

units.leftText: You know that Stephanas and his household were the first converts in Achaia, and they have devoted themselves to the service of the saints. Now I urge you, brothers,
units.rightText: Now I beseech you, brethren (ye know the house of Stephanas, that it is the firstfruits of Achaia, and that they have set themselves to minister unto the saints),

units.leftText: to submit to such as these, and to every fellow worker and laborer.
units.rightText: that ye also be in subjection unto such, and to every one that helpeth in the work and laboreth.

units.leftText: I am glad that Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus have arrived, because they have supplied what was lacking from you.
units.rightText: And I rejoice at the coming of Stephanas and Fortunatus and Achaicus: for that which was lacking on your part they supplied.

units.leftText: For they refreshed my spirit and yours as well. Show your appreciation, therefore, to such men. Signature and Final Greetings (Colossians 4:15–18|COL 4:15-18*; 2 Thessalonians 3:16–18|2TH 3:16-18*)
units.rightText: For they refreshed my spirit and yours: acknowledge ye therefore them that are such.

units.leftText: The churches in the province of Asia send you greetings. Aquila and Prisca greet you warmly in the Lord, and so does the church that meets at their house.
units.rightText: The churches of Asia salute you. Aquila and Prisca salute you much in the Lord, with the church that is in their house.
leftNotes: 16:19 Literally in Asia; Asia was a Roman province in what is now western Turkey.
16:19 Prisca is a variant of Priscilla; see Acts 18:2|ACT 18:2*.

units.leftText: All the brothers here send you greetings. Greet one another with a holy kiss.
units.rightText: All the brethren salute you. Salute one another with a holy kiss.

units.leftText: This greeting is in my own hand — Paul.
units.rightText: The salutation of me Paul with mine own hand.

units.leftText: If anyone does not love the Lord, let him be under a curse. Come, O Lord!
units.rightText: If any man loveth not the Lord, let him be anathema. Maranatha.
leftNotes: 16:22 Greek Marana Tha! from a transliteration of the Aramaic, an exclamation of approaching divine judgment

units.leftText: The grace of the Lord Jesus be with you.
units.rightText: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with you.

units.leftText: My love be with all of you in Christ Jesus. Amen.
units.rightText: My love be with you all in Christ Jesus. Amen.
leftNotes: 16:24 SBL, WH, and NA do not include Amen.
